records.issue_text: Success-path else branch increments retryCount even when SMS was scheduled successfully, making the counter semantically wrong
records.rationale: The diff shows `retryCount` is incremented only in the `else` branch of `if (scheduledSMS.sid) { ... }`, i.e., when there is **no** `sid` (not a successful schedule), and in the `catch` block on error. The contradicting detail is: `if (scheduledSMS.sid) { ... } else { ... retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`, so the increment does not occur on the success path.
records.stripped_text: Success-path else branch increments retryCount even when SMS was scheduled successfully, making the counter semantically wrong

records.issue_text: Unguarded prisma.workflowReminder.update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron handler, skipping remaining reminders
records.rationale: The diff adds an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch (error)` block (and also in the `else` branch) without any additional guarding. If that update throws (e.g., record missing, DB connectivity issue), the exception will escape the catch block and can abort the handler/loop, potentially skipping remaining reminders. This failure mode is directly introduced by the new update calls in the catch path.
records.stripped_text: Unguarded prisma.workflowReminder.update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole cron handler, skipping remaining reminders

records.issue_text: The retryCount > 1 deletion gate runs without a scheduledDate guard, deleting reminders that failed scheduling twice before their send window arrives, so customers never receive the SMS
records.rationale: The diff changes the cleanup deleteMany to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`, where the `retryCount > 1` branch has no `scheduledDate` (or even `method`) constraint. Since the loop increments `retryCount` on failures (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`), any reminder that has failed twice will be deleted on the next run regardless of whether its `scheduledDate` is still in the future, which can prevent the SMS from ever being sent.

records.issue_text: catch block increments retryCount for every error including transient Twilio config and network errors, so reminders can be permanently deleted due to infrastructure failures
records.rationale: The diff adds unconditional retry counting on failures: in the `catch (error)` block it always updates `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, and reminders with `retryCount > 1` are then deleted by `deleteMany` via `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` (note the retryCount condition has no further scoping). This means any repeated transient/infrastructure error during scheduling can increment `retryCount` and lead to permanent deletion of the reminder after >1 retries, matching the finding’s data-loss concern.
